title: Your Move: Escape the City Before It Falls

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: The last helicopter out of the city lifts off in ten seconds.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: And five hundred dead are between you and it.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Below you, the whole city is burning. And you are one jump from getting out.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Twenty four hours ago, you were asleep. Every choice from here is your move. Get them right, and you live.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Here's how this works. Every chapter, you get one choice. Pause the video, pick your move, and keep count. At the end, we'll see if you made it.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Six A.M. Every phone in the city screams at once.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You run to the window. Down on the street, people are running. And some of the people chasing them are not people anymore.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: On the news, a reporter is mid sentence when something pulls her off camera.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Across the street, a building is on fire. Then your power cuts out.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: And someone is pounding on your door. Not knocking. Pounding.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You've got about ten seconds to think. So you think about what matters. Water. Food. A way out.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: The door frame cracks.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your move. Barricade the door? Or grab your bag and run, right now?

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you barricaded, you're safe. For an hour. Then the smoke from across the street fills your floor.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You crawl to the window to breathe. Twelve floors up. No way down. And the door is still blocked by everything you own.

paper.title: FIRE FACT
paper.src: smoke inhalation causes the majority of fire deaths (U.S. fire safety data)

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Most people who die in fires never touch a flame. It's the smoke that gets them.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you ran, good move. You open the door just as your neighbor lunges. He's already turned.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: He flies past you, into your apartment. You slam the door behind him.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You grab the bag you packed for camping last summer. Water bottle. Flashlight. Knife. First aid kit.

paper.title: RULE ONE
paper.src: evacuation guidance: leave early, before routes are blocked

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Rule one of any emergency. Don't wait for someone to tell you to leave.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: The hallway lights are flashing red. Fire alarm. And somewhere below you, someone is screaming.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your building has twelve floors. And the elevator still works.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your move. The elevator? Or the stairs?

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you took the elevator, it stops between floors four and five. Then the doors start to open. From the outside.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Grey fingers slide through the gap. Then a face. Then another. You're in a steel box, and they're opening it.

paper.title: EMERGENCY RULE
paper.src: standard fire and emergency evacuation guidance

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: In an emergency, never take the elevator. When the power goes, it becomes a steel box with no way out.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you took the stairs, good move. But ten floors down, the dead are already coming up.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: So you do what you did as a kid. You slide down the railing, straight over their heads.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your hands burn. Your bag almost rips off your back. But you're moving faster than anything on those stairs.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: The lobby. And the front door is locked.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: So you rip the fire extinguisher off the wall, and you swing.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You hit the lobby running, and go straight through the glass door.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Seven A.M. The highway out of the city is one giant parking lot. Ten thousand cars. Nobody's moving.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Car doors hang open. Engines still running. People left everything and ran.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Somewhere behind you, a truck horn is stuck on. Nobody is left to let go of it.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: And the dead are walking between the lanes.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: So you run across the roofs. Car to car to car.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Then a car alarm goes off under your feet. A hundred and twenty decibels.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Every head on the highway turns toward you.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You've got maybe forty seconds before they reach you.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your move. Steal the motorcycle next to you? Or keep going on foot?

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you took the motorcycle, the keys aren't in it. You lose forty seconds. That's all they need.

paper.title: NOISE = DANGER
paper.src: in a quiet city, engine noise carries for blocks

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Engines are loud. On a silent highway, an engine is a dinner bell.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you kept going on foot, good move. You drop off the side of the road, and down into the subway.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Ten seconds after you disappear down the stairs, the first of them reaches the car where you were standing.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Eight thirty. The subway is pitch black. Your flashlight is the only light underground.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Somewhere in the dark, water is dripping. And every drop sounds like footsteps.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Then your flashlight catches something on the tracks ahead. It's moving. It's a rat. Hundreds of them. All running the same way.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Then you hear it. A train. Running on its own. Nobody driving.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You press flat against the wall as it screams past, three inches from your face.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: In the windows, you see faces. Pressed against the glass. Not one of them is blinking.

paper.title: THE THIRD RAIL
paper.src: subway third rails typically carry about 600-750 volts DC

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Down here, the rail next to the tracks carries over six hundred volts. One step on it, and it's over.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Then the tunnel splits.

beats.opt2: Follow the rats along the ledge
beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your move. Follow the tracks? Or follow the rats along the ledge?

beats.opt2: Follow the rats along the ledge

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you followed the tracks, a second train comes. And there's nowhere to stand but the third rail.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Six hundred volts or a train. There's no good way out of that tunnel.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you followed the rats, good move. Rats run from danger, and they always know the way up.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Two hundred yards later, daylight through a grate. A ladder. Up.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Ten A.M. The tunnel comes up under City Hospital.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: The emergency room doors are wide open. Gurneys everywhere. Nobody behind the desk.

paper.title: WHY YOU NEED MEDICINE
paper.src: before penicillin (1940s), infected wounds were a leading cause of death

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your arm is cut from the glass door. Out here, one infected cut can kill you.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: The lights flicker. And at the end of the corridor stands a surgeon. Still in his mask.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: He runs at you. You kick a gurney straight down the hall into him.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: He goes down. He doesn't stay down. You don't wait to see more.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your move. The pharmacy? Or the blood bank?

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you picked the blood bank, the smell of blood wakes up the whole ward. They come out of every room.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Ten doors. Ten of them. And you're standing in the middle of the hall.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you picked the pharmacy, good move. Antibiotics, bandages, painkillers. You clean the cut, and you go.

paper.title: WOUND CARE
paper.src: basic first aid for minor cuts and scrapes

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: The right way to treat a cut out here. Clean it with clean water. Press to stop the bleeding. Cover it. Change it every day.

paper.title: HALFWAY CHECK
paper.src: keep count - your final score is at the end

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Halfway. Five moves down. If you got all five right, you're already doing better than most of this city.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Noon. The mall. Every exit is chained shut, but the sports store is wide open.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You grab gloves, a helmet, and a bottle of water from a cooler that still feels cold.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Then the escalator starts moving. And it's full of them.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: They tumble down the steps on top of each other. Twenty of them. And more behind.

paper.title: SPEED MATH
lines: THE DEAD: AS FAST AS YOU
paper.src: typical jogging and casual cycling speeds

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: A person can run about six miles an hour. On a bike, you can do fifteen.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your move. Grab a bike? Or a skateboard?

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you took the skateboard, the wheels catch on broken glass, and you go flying.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You hit the tile hard. And by the time you look up, they're already on you.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you took the bike, good move. You ride it straight through the food court, and out the loading dock.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Behind you, the food court tables go flying as they chase. But on two wheels, you are gone.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: The loading dock door is jammed halfway. You duck flat on the handlebars and slide right under it.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Three P.M. The streets are blocked, so you go up. Roof to roof.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: From up here, you can see the whole city. Smoke in every direction. And one helicopter circling a tower downtown.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You clear one gap. Then another.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Twice, your foot slips on loose gravel. Twice, you catch yourself.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Then the next gap is twelve feet. With a bag on your back, you'll make eight. Maybe.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your move. Jump it anyway? Or use the window cleaner's rope across the gap?

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you jumped, you hit the far wall, and you hang by your fingertips. Right above them.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your fingers slip one at a time. And sixty feet below, they're waiting with their arms up.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you took the rope, good move. Hand over hand, over sixty feet of nothing.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your arms are shaking when you reach the other side. But you're across. And they're not.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Five P.M. The river bridge. The only way across. And it's packed. A thousand dead, shoulder to shoulder.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Cars bumper to bumper. And between them, every one of the dead is facing your way.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your move. Push through on the bridge? Or jump into the river?

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you pushed through, you make it forty feet. Then hands grab your bag, and pull you down.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: A thousand of them. One of you. The bridge was never a path. It was a trap.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you jumped, good move. Feet first. Arms crossed. Body straight.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You hit the water like a pencil. It's so cold, it punches the air right out of your lungs.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Cold water has a rule. One minute to control your breathing. Ten minutes before your arms quit. One hour before you pass out.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You float. You breathe. And you let the current carry you to the far bank.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You crawl out on the far bank, soaked and freezing. Wet clothes pull heat out of your body way faster than air.

paper.title: WET = COLD
paper.src: water conducts heat roughly 25 times faster than air

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Water steals your body heat about twenty five times faster than air. So you wring out every layer, and you keep moving.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Behind you, on the bridge, a thousand heads watch you go. Not one of them follows you into the water.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Seven P.M. Searchlights. A military checkpoint. Soldiers checking everyone for bites.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: A soldier with a megaphone. Hands where we can see them. One at a time.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You have a scratch on your arm. From the glass. Not a bite. But they can't know that.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: The soldier's flashlight stops on your arm.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your move. Tell them about the scratch? Or hide it?

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you hid it, they find it anyway. To them, hidden means bitten. The gate closes in your face.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Through the fence, you can see the tents, the lights, the hot food. And you're on the wrong side of it.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you told them, good move. The medic checks it, cleans it, and waves you through.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Behind the fence, tents, lights, hot food. And a sign. Last helicopter, nine P.M.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You look at your watch. Eight fifty. You run.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Ten floors of stairs. Your legs are burning. Then the roof door.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Eight fifty nine P.M. The roof of the evacuation tower. The last helicopter is already lifting.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: And the stairwell door bursts open behind you. Five hundred of them.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Your move. Jump for the ladder? Or wait for the next helicopter?

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you waited, there is no next one.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: The sound of the rotors fades. And all five hundred of them turn to look at you.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: If you jumped, good move. Your fingers close around the last rung. And the city falls away beneath you.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: For one second, the ladder swings out over nothing but fire. You don't let go.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: You made it.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Below you, the city goes dark, one block at a time. Twenty four hours. Ten moves. And you're still breathing.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Now count your moves. Ten out of ten, you're a legend. Seven or more, you survived. Under five, you'd be one of them.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: Comment your score. And subscribe, because your next move is coming.

beats.name: NARRATOR
beats.text: And tell me which move almost got you.
